notes: The box flaps. Same kraft family as `cardboard` and the same v2 correction — the flaps are most of the kart's screen area in every capture, so they were carrying most of the amoeba camouflage the critique measured. Held about a stop below the body so the open rim still reads as a rim: the flaps splay out past the silhouette and need a value break against the deck, not just an outline. brushScale is a little finer than the body's (2.2 against 2.6) so the two do not mottle in lockstep, but both sit below the LOD ladder's floor and are therefore world-locked rather than screen-locked. The corrugated cut along the free edge is geometry — see `flapGeometry` in src/vehicle/box.ts. Brush overlay reduced 0.2 -> 0.18: the painterly direction is abandoned (ART_BIBLE 1) and this was still running at full strength, which is the camouflage mottle on terrain. v3 DROPS THE LIT AND TOP STOPS so a folded flap reads as the same board as the wall it lies on. Measured on car-corner, the folded side flap rendered #e4bd7b V0.89 against the wall's #c0925a V0.75 — a 0.14 step, making the band the brightest thing on the entire vehicle, where the reference draws it at V0.75 against a V0.71 wall and it is barely distinguishable. Flattening the fold from 17 degrees off the wall to 7 changed the figure by nothing, which is what identified the real cause: a flap is a FLAT SLAB with one normal across its whole face, so it selects a single ramp stop over that whole area, while the wall is a lofted tub carrying flutes and corner creases and therefore averages several. The same mechanism darkened the steering wheel's spokes two rounds earlier. Scaled by 0.84, which is the ratio the measurement asks for. The END flaps share this surface and go darker with it — correct, since the sheet's end flaps are seen edge-on and read slightly darker than the box too.
